Bachelor's degree in related area and / or equivalent experience / training.
Demonstrated experience administering enterprise, compliance, or assessment technology platforms, including vendor coordination, configuration, and process documentation.
Experience in student conduct, academic integrity administration, test security, or a closely related compliance or student services function, preferably in an online learning environment.

Demonstrated growth mindset toward emerging technologies, with experience or willingness to explore and adopt AI-powered tools to enhance productivity, support data-driven decision-making, and drive continuous improvement in workflows and outcomes.
Experience teaching or working directly with secondary students in an online or blended setting.
Experience administering proctoring, plagiarism detection, or identity verification systems, including platforms such as Honorlock or Turnitin, and working within a student information system.

The Academic Integrity Specialist serves as UC Scout's primary subject matter expert on academic integrity policy, student identity verification, and integrity-related technology. The position approaches academic integrity as both a protective and a developmental function, safeguarding the credibility of UC Scout credit while helping students build the habits of authentic scholarship that will serve them in college, career, and life. The person in this role works to sustain a course culture in which original, honest work is the expected and supported norm.

The Specialist works within an academic integrity framework established by UC Scout leadership, applying it consistently across cases and exercising judgment that accounts for the age and developmental stage of the program's middle and high school students. Responses to academic dishonesty are expected to be proportionate to the violation, instructive wherever possible, and resolved at the lowest appropriate level.

The Academic Integrity Specialist is responsible for managing escalated academic integrity cases, including incidents involving repeated or egregious violations. In these cases, the Specialist conducts thorough, impartial investigations; meets with students and their families; and determines appropriate consequences on a case-by-case basis, in alignment with UC Scout policy. Given the position's regular direct contact with minors, the Specialist adheres to protocols for student meetings. The Specialist also determines when a case warrants referral to the Student Academic Review Committee, the program's final tier of review for the most serious violations. This work requires exceptional judgment, professional discretion, and the ability to facilitate difficult conversations with students, families, and staff with clarity and care. The Specialist may be asked to assist with other escalated student or family matters referred by the Academic Director, applying the same investigative and de-escalation skills.

The Specialist serves as the program's subject matter expert on identity verification and assessment security, and as the primary point of contact for proctoring, plagiarism detection, and related technology vendors. This includes evaluating emerging integrity technologies, monitoring for unauthorized distribution of UC Scout course content, and pursuing removal of protected course materials from third-party sites.

Beyond case management and operations, the Academic Integrity Specialist contributes meaningfully to the long-term health of UC Scout's academic environment. This includes developing and collaborating on integrity-focused training for UC Scout instructors; creating student-facing content and campaigns that make expectations clear and celebrate authentic learning and ethical AI use; collaborating with instructional design and academic staff to shape course and assessment practices that reduce opportunities for dishonesty; and keeping policy current as generative AI and student behavior continue to evolve.
High degree of personal and professional integrity, with demonstrated respect for student privacy, confidentiality, and due process.
Selected candidate will be required to pass a pre-employment criminal history background check.
Selected candidate must pass the employment misconduct disclosure process.
Must reside within the State of California.
This is a fully remote position, and the selected candidate must be able to work successfully from a home/remote office and be able to fulfill the requirements of the UCSC telecommuting agreement.
Selected candidate will be required to complete training within established time frames as directed including UC compliance training.

The University of California has implemented a Vaccination Policy covering all employees. Employees, including new hires, are required to comply with any applicable policies relating to the University of California vaccine program.

Per the Child Abuse and Neglect Reporting Act (CANRA), this position has been identified as a Mandated Reporter. The selected candidate will be required to report known or suspected child abuse or neglect as defined by CANRA and will be required to sign a Statement Acknowledging Requirement to Report Child Abuse prior to commencing employment. CANRA Penal Codes, and related definitions, requirements, and responsibilities may be obtained here.

Exercise the utmost discretion in managing sensitive information learned in the course of performing their duties. Sensitive information includes but is not limited to employee and student records, health and patient records, financial data, strategic plans, proprietary information, and any other sensitive or non-public information learned during the course and scope of employment. Understands that sensitive information should be shared on a limited basis and actively takes steps to limit access to sensitive information to individuals who have legitimate business need to know. Ensure that sensitive information is properly safeguarded. Follow all organizational policies and laws on data protection and privacy. This includes secure handling of physical and digital records and proper usage of IT systems to prevent data leaks. The unauthorized or improper disclosure of confidential work-related information obtained from any source on any work-related matter is a violation of these expectations.
Working knowledge of academic integrity principles and practices in secondary or higher education, including emerging challenges related to generative AI and online assessment.
Ability to work long periods of time at a computer with or without accommodation.

Strong written communication skills, with demonstrated ability to produce clear case documentation, policy language, and correspondence that withstand review and appeal, and to manage a dynamic and confidential caseload to deadline.
Ability to work occasional evenings and weekends as directed.

Demonstrated ability to conduct impartial investigations and reach defensible, evidence-based conclusions in ambiguous or contested situations, and to apply established institutional policy consistently and equitably, including in circumstances where the individual's personal judgment may differ from the applicable standard.
Ability to travel nationally.

Understanding of adolescent development and demonstrated ability to respond to academic dishonesty by minors in a manner that is proportionate, instructive, and oriented toward the student's continued learning.
Ability to maintain appearance and conduct suitable for working in a professional setting.

Ability to facilitate sensitive, high-stakes conversations virtually - and occasionally outside standard hours - with students, families, and staff with professionalism, empathy, and clarity, and to exercise restraint and sound judgment in high-emotion situations by de-escalating conflict and resolving matters at the lowest appropriate level.
